meta.title: Prescription dosage validation
meta.disclaimer: Every entity, name, identifier and threshold in this file is synthetic and invented for QAIA test purposes. Drug names are fictional. Nothing here is real clinical guidance or a real drug reference, and no numeric threshold here may be used as medical advice or as a source of clinical fact.
meta.pii: none — no real individual is represented; identifiers are opaque codes, not names

entities.drug: reference record — AC1: minEffective, maxPerIntake, maxCumulative24h, ageFloorYears
entities.prescriber: AC5 role, AC2/AC7 identity for the audit trail
entities.intake: AC4 — a dated administration of a drug to a patient, the rows the 24 h window sums

drugs.note: nominal record — the Background of every feature file
incomplete record: no age floor — feeds C03 / @QAIA-US-002-003, open question Q7
ODD maxPerIntake: halving it under AC6 has no stated rounding rule — feeds C19 / @QAIA-US-002-019, question Q6

max < 2 x min: under AC6 the reduced maximum (7.5) falls BELOW the minimum effective dose (10). Every dose is then both under the minimum and over the maximum. Feeds C20 / @QAIA-US-002-020, question Q4 — the triple contradiction AC2 x AC6 x AC3
deliberately has NO reference record — feeds C02 / @QAIA-US-002-002, question Q7

patients.note: renal modifier only — the metamorphic pair partner of P1 (C18)
one year below DRUG-A's age floor — C14, C16, C17
exactly at the age floor — C15
BOTH modifiers at once — C21, question Q5

prescribers.note: second actor, required only by the concurrency case C13

intakeHistory.note: C12 — straddles midnight: inside a rolling 24 h window, outside a calendar day. Question Q3

cases.why: maxPerIntake 7 halved = 3.5; 4 is above it whichever way 3.5 rounds — chosen so the case stays decidable despite the missing rounding rule

cases.assumption: Q10 — counted in Unicode code points after trimming

notGenerated.doseUnit: AC1..AC6 never name a unit. Every amount above is stated in mg because DRUG-A's record is, but the source does not license that choice — open question Q2. A dataset cannot resolve it; it can only avoid pretending it did.
notGenerated.clockReference: intakeHistory uses offsets from the moment of prescription, which presumes a ROLLING window. A calendar-day reading would need different rows. Question Q3 — the dataset is therefore valid for one of the two readings only, and says which.
